---
title: "About"
---

## What this site is

Physics by Construction is a course site about physics, programming, and
proof. Lessons are ordered along one path of increasing difficulty: mechanics
with numerical simulation first, then experiments driven by AI agents, then
formal proofs in Lean.

## Who it is for

Readers who have undergraduate physics (classical mechanics, calculus, linear
algebra) and solid programming skills. Lessons state their prerequisites and
link out instead of repeating them.

## How the site is built

- Code shown in a lesson is code the build ran. Figures and numbers are the
  output of that code, regenerated on every build.
- Proofs are compiled by Lean on every change. A lesson whose code fails or
  whose proof does not compile cannot be published.
- Equations are MathML. Text, code, equations, and figures are readable with
  JavaScript turned off.
- The site is static files. It has no accounts, sets no cookies, runs no
  analytics, and loads nothing from other websites.

The [rendering check](rendering-check.qmd) page shows sample equations, code,
and a figure produced by this pipeline.
